utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Case Number IT-98-29-A, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the parties, please. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell, Ms. Helen Brady, and Ms. Susan Grogan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One forgets to put the microphone on. Good morning to everyone. My name is Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I represent Mr. Galic, and my assistant is present. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference according to Rule 65 bis. And the purpose of a Status Conference is really to find out the status of the proceedings and also to find out from the appellant his status of detention and whether there are any matters he wishes to raise with the Bench, bearing in mind of course the administrative procedures with the office of the registrar on any matters that fall within the Rules of Detention. This is the second Status Conference in this appeal. We had the first one on 31st March this year. And as the parties are in the process of exchanging procedural stages of the appeal, I have noted from the record that all the processes appear to be on time. In this appeal we also have a Rule 115 motion which is under consideration and the parties so far are complying within the deadlines. I wanted to find out from the parties whether there are any matters they wish to raise. On my way of -- the motion on record, which I deal with later. Is there any other matter besides the motion from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the Defence? Any other matter other than the motion that is on record that they wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that a while ago in order to save time the Trial Chamber wanted us to respond orally and not in writing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that is the case, I will respond immediately. Therefore, Your Honour, would you grant me two or three minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three minutes to look at the motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can do it if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I'll give the party -- the Defence three minutes, but before I do that I would like to raise this very motion with the Prosecution. I noticed that according to the Rules the respondent's brief, that is your response from the appellant's appeal is supposed to be filed on 30th of August this year. And your motion is applying for an extension of two weeks so that you file it on the 13th of September, 2004. Besides what you have stated in this motion as your reasons, what else is there? What else is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: If you'd like me to address that issue, the matters that are stated in the motion are pretty much comprehensive. The only other matter which was not places on the record, if you wish, is that some of the staff in the appeals section will be absent in the month of August, myself included. Presently I'm scheduled to be away the last two weeks of August. And those are the only matters that I can bring to your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see. The Prosecution is aware that when the court is in recess, that does not mean recess for procedural matters in criminal trials and appeals.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Of course not, and the Prosecution has complied for the last four summers with the filing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Especially since the parties know that the Judges do not go on recess in the sense that there is always a duty Judge to attend to matters. That shows that the Appeals Chamber, as well as Trial Chambers expect that procedural matters must continue because these are criminal trials and criminal appeals and nobody in their right senses would like to delay the proceedings simply because of a vacation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Absolutely not, Your Honour. If you'll note in paragraph 5, the primary basis for the extension is the one, two, three, four, five other filings, four of them during the recess and all of them the Prosecution is going to attempt to comply with in relation to those. We're not asking that there be a vacation of all filing deadlines for the whole summer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farrell, but you know all these cases have to go on and that all persons are equal before the Tribunal and so is this appellant and his appeal. So he cannot be delayed simply because the Prosecution's office has several other cases, just like the Appeals Chamber's Judges have several other cases. And all of us are doing our level best to beat, if not meet the deadlines. So you are equally bound by the Rules. There is nothing in the Rules to say that if the Prosecution's office is overloaded, then the extensions of time are right. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No doubt about that. And there are other reasons as well. First of all, the appellants had seven months in which to draft their brief. We're asking for two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because of the translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Sure enough, and the 145 pages, the extra 45 pages was -- certainly no other reason than volume.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Farrell, if the other party is a little weak procedurally, that doesn't mean -- that doesn't give the other party the right to be equally weak. The parties are asking to be diligent because we are quite loaded at the Tribunal. Anyway, I've understood your reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the Defence has had enough time to look at the motion and also have understood the Bench's concerns in this regard. So you are through.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready? The Bench is willing to give you time if you need it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. First of all, I'm not sure that the additional time we might have had would have resulted from -- the Defence's access is a result of the Tribunal's procedure. This procedure is organised in a way that the two texts, the English text and the French texts, were not drafted at the same time -- [In English] to do anything against this and this is a matter. Against what we have -- I mean, we must accept it. [Interpretation] Having raised that issue, as far as the motion itself is concerned we would like to say -- I would like to say the following. Firstly, there is a number of areas of the motion because I'm also aware of a decision of your Chamber dated the 21 July, 2004. And I'm not aware of an authorisation consisting of 143 [as interpreted] pages. But the reasons for the appeal have been known by the Prosecution for a long time. This was made known in our notice of appeal and the Prosecution was aware of all the items, all this as we had raised. We haven't added anything. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond I would like to thank the Chamber for having granted us additional pages and I would like apologise to -- on behalf of the entire Defence because we drafted the new text, 145 pages of new text. We did so very rapidly and as a result of certain errors, typing errors, layout errors, and we would like to apologise for that. We have listed the errors made and provided it to the Chamber and it will soon be provided to the Prosecution. When we have to work rapidly, the Defence doubts -- and the Defence team is not as numerous as the Prosecution's team. We also had to work over the summer. All the members of the Defence had to find time to work and we don't see why we should accept that the Prosecution should have additional time because they want to have a nice summer period. That is all the more the case because when we asked the Prosecution whether we could ask -- make a joint request for additional pages, this request was refused for the same reasons. So equality of arms means that this motion should be refused. I thank you in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you counsel for the Defence. I've noted your concerns, and all I can say is that Defence counsel are expected to work outright once they accept a brief, either at trial or on appeal. This is expected of lawyers in practice. They cannot hold their client's liberty to ransom simply because they have no time or they are too busy if that were the case. Nobody who has a busy schedule should accept a brief in this Tribunal. It's no excuse saying that there is no time for that, there is no time for that. Because when the practice directions were issued, they were very well thought out and that the Appeals Chamber does expect that parties that will accept appeal briefs are committed to duty and will comply with the times, subject of course to translation difficulties which we are all aware of and which the Appeals Chamber almost always does give deference to because the Tribunal cannot meet the weight load on time in the translation unit. Having heard the Defence and with my prior remarks on the request by the Prosecution, I will deal with the matter right away. I accept the concerns raised by the Prosecution, but like I said the practice directions must not be undermined by lame excuses as a busy work schedule. This Tribunal has had a busy work schedule right from day one and it is expected of all of us to meet our deadlines and targets. I also note what the Defence have said, but I believe that in the interests of justice and also to state that during the pre-trial -- pre-appeal proceedings, the Appeals Chamber does try very hard to allow the parties sufficient time so that they can file in the best pleadings possible and this does assist the Appeals Chamber itself in dealing with the appeals before it. So I will grant -- the Prosecution have the time they've asked for. And the Defence filing their respondent's brief on the 10th, they should file it by the 6th of September. That is extra working days which are granted in view of their plea. The written decision will be filed in due course. I would like now to turn to the appellant, Mr. Galic, and find out his status. Mr. Galic, are there any matters you wish to raise regarding your health, regarding your detention facilities, or any other matter concerning this appeal? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Thank you for giving me this opportunity to address you. Very briefly, since the last Status Conference my spine was x-rayed or scanned on the 16th of June in the Bronovo Hospital. And when they compared the 2001 x-ray and the present x-ray, the conclusion they came to was that the condition my spine is in is gradually deteriorating. We'll see what will happen in the future. But apart from that, everything is quite normal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Galic. You may be seated. The Bench is glad to note that the necessary medical attention is being received by yourself, and we can only hope that your health does not deteriorate and that should be another factor to urge the parties to comply with the deadlines, so that as much as possible this appeal can be heard before the end of this year so that the appellant can have the final decision on this case and that will I'm sure be a positive factor as far as his health is concerned. Any other matters? The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Defence, any matters you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There being no other matters, this Status Conference has come to an end and the court will rise. ---Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at 8.47 a.m. 23 24 25
